theory.intro: The **product** is the answer when you multiply numbers together. The numbers being multiplied are called factors.
facts: Changing the order does not change the product: $4 \times 6=6 \times 4$.
You can multiply more than two numbers, e.g. $2 \times 3 \times 5 = 30$.
Grouping the factors differently does not change the product. A useful pair can make the calculation easier.
steps: Identify the numbers (factors) to be multiplied.
Multiply the factors, two at a time. You can choose a useful pair to multiply first.

workedExamples.question_text:
Write “the product of $6$ and $13$ is $78$” as a multiplication.
Which numbers are the factors, and which is the product?
workedExamples.solution_text:
$6 \times 13=78$
The factors are $6$ and $13$. The product is $78$.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) Find $13 \times 4 \times 25$ by choosing a useful pair of factors.
(b) Does $25 \times 13 \times 4$ have the same product? Explain.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $13 \times 4 \times 25$
$=13 \times (4 \times 25)$
$=13 \times 100$
$=1300$
(b) Yes. The same factors are in a different order, so the product is also $1300$.
